look.text: It doesn't run. It doesn't growl. It stands with its head low, fur grey as old ash, and its eyes are empty: no shine in them at all. Burnt into its flank is a mark, a circle split by three lines. You copy it onto a scrap of hide with charcoal from your pack.

choices.text: Put it out of its misery.

again.text: It hasn't moved. It might not have moved since you left it.

choices.text: Put it out of its misery.

tracks.text: The same prints you've followed for three days: no stride, no hunting, straight lines through brush a wolf would go round. They don't start at the den. They come from the north, out of the forest, as if something walked it here and let go.

choices.text: Put it out of its misery.

mark_scholar.text: Not a brand. The skin isn't scarred, it's emptied, as if the mark had been drawn by taking something out rather than burning something in. You've read about drawing power from a living thing. Every book you've read about it was a warning.

choices.text: Put it out of its misery.

mercy.text: It doesn't fight you. When it falls, a thread of pale light rises from the mark, thin as spider silk, and drifts away north until you lose it against the sky.

leave.text: When you look back, it's still standing there, facing nothing.
